arxiv-2011-10089.title: Jammed disks of two sizes in a narrow channel
arxiv-2011-10089.creator: Dan Liu and Gerhard Müller
arxiv-2011-10089.description: Abstract A granular-matter model is exactly solved, where disks of two sizes and weights in alternating sequence are confined to a narrow channel. The axis of the channel is horizontal and its plane vertical. Disk sizes and channel width are such that under jamming no disks remain loose and all disks touch one wall.

arxiv-2106-10123.title: Challenges and Limitations with the Metrics Measuring the Complexity of Code-Mixed Text
arxiv-2106-10123.creator: Vivek Srivastava, Mayank Singh
arxiv-2106-10123.description: Abstract Code-mixing is a frequent communication style among multilingual speakers where they mix words and phrases from two different languages in the same utterance of text or speech. Identifying and filtering code-mixed text is a challenging task due to its co-existence with monolingual and noisy text.

arxiv-2212-02384.title: Addressing Distribution Shift at Test Time in Pre-trained Language Models
arxiv-2212-02384.creator: Ayush Singh, John E. Ortega
arxiv-2212-02384.description: Abstract State-of-the-art pre-trained language models (PLMs) outperform other models when applied to the majority of language processing tasks. However, PLMs have been found to degrade in performance under distribution shift, a phenomenon that occurs when data at test-time does not come from the same distribution as the source training set.

arxiv-2504-08267.title: Left-Right Symmetric Neutrino Mass Model without Scalar Bi-doublet
arxiv-2504-08267.creator: Zafri A. Borboruah, Lekhika Malhotra, Utkarsh Patel, Sudhanwa Patra, S. Uma Sankar
arxiv-2504-08267.description: Abstract We consider a left-right symmetric model with an S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) L SU(2)_{L} and an S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) R SU(2)_{R} scalar doublet but without the scalar bidoublet. The charged fermion masses in this model are generated via a universal seesaw mechanism.

arxiv-2505-12856.title: Addressing memory bandwidth scalability in vector processors for streaming applications
arxiv-2505-12856.creator: Jordi Altayó, Paul Delestrac, Ahmed Hemani, David Novo, Simey Yang, Debjyoti Bhattacharjee, Francky Cathoor
arxiv-2505-12856.description: Abstract . As the size of artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) models and datasets grows, the memory bandwidth becomes a critical bottleneck. The paper presents a novel extended memory hierarchy that addresses some major memory bandwidth challenges in data-parallel AI/ML applications.

arxiv-2602-13576.title: Rubrics as an Attack Surface: Stealthy Preference Drift in LLM Judges
arxiv-2602-13576.creator: Ruomeng Ding, Yifei Pang *, He Sun, Yizhong Wang, Zhiwei Steven Wu, Zhun Deng
arxiv-2602-13576.description: Abstract Evaluation and alignment pipelines for large language models increasingly rely on LLM-based judges, whose behavior is guided by natural-language rubrics and validated on benchmarks. We identify a previously under-recognized vulnerability in this workflow, which we term Rubric-Induced Preference Drift ( RIPD ).

arxiv-2602-18498.title: Evolution of fairness in hybrid populations with specialised AI agents
arxiv-2602-18498.creator: Zhao Song 1, Theodor Cimpeanu 2, Chen Shen 3 and The Anh Han 1
arxiv-2602-18498.description: Abstract Fairness in hybrid societies hinges on a simple choice: should AI be a generous host or a strict gatekeeper? Moving beyond symmetric models, we show that asymmetric social structures–like those in hiring, regulation, and negotiation–AI that guards fairness outperforms AI that gifts it.

pmc-10705026.creator: Adediwura Oladunni Arowosegbe, Iyabode Olabisi Dedeke, Olufunke Bolatito Shittu, David Ajiboye Ojo, Joy Stephen Amusan, Opeoluwa Iwaloye, Uwemedimo Friday Ekpo
